_doc: Where a reader marked Mattie Williamson's facial landmarks on her 1890s portrait, in pixels of the crop `crop_px` (left, top, right, bottom) of the blog's original-size copy. The light comes from her left (the reader's right), so her right eye (the reader's left) is in deep shadow: its corners carry wide uncertainties. Her face is near frontal, turned a little to her left; her right ear is lost in her hair's shadow, so the LEFT ear (the reader's right, an earring at its lobe) is marked, its top under her hair. The mouth is the lips' meeting line; the chin's lower edge is where the lit chin meets her collar's shadow. `base_body` fits against her own body's rest face. tools/fit_portrait_face.py fits the face to these marks.
age_note: The portrait is captioned 'in the 1890s'; her leg-o'-mutton sleeves date it to about 1893-1897, and she was born in October 1859, so she was about 36. The renderer's ageing pair takes her to 44 at the scene date.
basis: Fitted to a photograph of her showing her whole face (her 1890s portrait, published by the Glessner House museum): the eye spacing, nose, mouth, chin and ear placement are read from it, against her own body's face, as far as the shared MakeHuman face axes can express them. Depth is read from a single near-frontal view, so an axis the marks say little about stays near her body's own (listed as mostly_prior).
not_modelled: her colouring (the portrait is sepia; skin and hair colours are chosen)
her hair as she wore it (dark, wavy, centre-parted and drawn up; the model wears the town's bun)

card._doc: What the person's card shows (T-3486, as T-3413): `portrait` is cut from the copy at `portrait_from_scan_px` and scaled to `size_px` (tools/cut_portrait.py); `model` is tools/portrait_still.mjs's render of the fitted face on `body`, turned to the fit's yaw, dressed as humans.js dresses her in town.
